question: Article 368 is related to the amendment of the Constitution, it is covered under which part of the constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: 20th
13th
21th
18th
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 20th Part

Explanation:
Article 368 of the Indian Constitution deals with the procedure for amending the Constitution and falls under Part XX (20th Part). This article empowers the Parliament to amend the Constitution through a process that may require a simple majority, special majority, or ratification by states. Part XX contains only one article, Article 368, which outlines the amendment process while preserving the basic structure of the Constitution. The Supreme Court, in the Kesavananda Bharati case, established that the Parliament cannot alter the basic structure. Thus, Article 368 serves as the guide for constitutional amendments, ensuring flexibility while protecting core principles.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Which part of the Constitution contains Article 368? → Part XX
☛ What is Article 368 related to? → Amendment of the Constitution
☛ Which case propounded the basic structure doctrine? → Kesavananda Bharati
☛ What type of majority is required for amending the Constitution? → Special majority
☛ How many parts are there in the Indian Constitution? → 22 parts
question_hi: अनुच्छेद 368 संविधान संशोधन से संबंधित है, यह संविधान के किस भाग के अंतर्गत आता है? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: 20th
13th
21th
18th
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है 20वाँ भाग

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 368 संविधान संशोधन की प्रक्रिया से संबंधित है और यह संविधान के भाग XX (20वें भाग) के अंतर्गत आता है। यह अनुच्छेद संसद को संविधान में संशोधन करने की शक्ति प्रदान करता है, जिसमें साधारण बहुमत से लेकर विशेष बहुमत और राज्यों के अनुमोदन की आवश्यकता होती है। भाग XX में केवल एक ही अनुच्छेद है, जो अनुच्छेद 368 है। यह संविधान के मूल ढांचे को बनाए रखते हुए संशोधन की प्रक्रिया निर्धारित करता है। सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने केशवानंद भारती मामले में कहा कि संसद संविधान के मूल ढांचे में बदलाव नहीं कर सकती। इस प्रकार, अनुच्छेद 368 संविधान संशोधन के लिए मार्गदर्शक है।

question: On whose approval can the Lok Sabha be dissolved by the President?  (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Chief Justice of India
Parliament
Prime Minister
Chief Secretary of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Prime Minister

Explanation:
Under Article 85 of the Indian Constitution, the President can dissolve the Lok Sabha on the advice of the Prime Minister. The Prime Minister heads the Council of Ministers, and his advice is binding on the President as per Article 74. The Lok Sabha normally has a term of 5 years, but the President can dissolve it prematurely only on the Prime Minister's recommendation. The Chief Justice of India, Parliament, or Chief Secretary have no authority in this matter. This power ensures that the executive remains accountable to the legislature.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who has the power to dissolve Lok Sabha? → President on PM's advice
☛ Article 85 deals with? → Sessions, prorogation, and dissolution of Parliament
☛ Article 74 states? → President is bound by Council of Ministers' advice
☛ Maximum term of Lok Sabha? → 5 years
☛ On whose recommendation does President dissolve Lok Sabha? → Prime Minister

question: How is India defined by Article 1 of Indian Constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: As an uncontrollable colony
Disruptive Union
As a union of states
As Disruptive Colonizer
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is As a union of states

Explanation:
Article 1 of the Indian Constitution describes India as a 'Union of States'. The term 'Union' signifies the indestructible unity of India, rather than a federal structure based on a treaty. The Constituent Assembly deliberately chose 'Union' over 'Federation' because it does not grant states the right to secede. Article 1 states that 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States'. This provision is part of Part I of the Constitution, which deals with the Union and its territory. India is an indestructible Union where states have no constitutional right to alter their boundaries or existence. The phrase 'Union of States' emphasizes the permanent and indissoluble nature of the Indian federation.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Article 1 defines India as what? → A Union of States
☛ Which part of the Constitution deals with the Union and its territory? → Part I
☛ Which Article contains 'Union of States'? → Article 1
☛ What type of Union is India? → Indestructible
☛ Do states have the right to secede? → No
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 1 द्वारा भारत को कैसे परिभाषित किया गया है? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)

विघटनकारी संघ
राज्यों के संघ के रूप में

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 1 भारत को 'राज्यों के संघ' के रूप में वर्णित करता है। यह 'संघ' शब्द भारत की अविभाज्य एकता को दर्शाता है, न कि किसी संधि या समझौते पर आधारित संघीय ढांचे को। संविधान सभा ने जानबूझकर 'फेडरेशन' के बजाय 'यूनियन' शब्द चुना, क्योंकि यह राज्यों को अलग होने का अधिकार नहीं देता। अनुच्छेद 1 में कहा गया है कि 'इंडिया, दैट इज़ भारत, शैल बी अ यूनियन ऑफ स्टेट्स'। यह संविधान के भाग 1 के अंतर्गत आता है, जो संघ और उसके क्षेत्र को परिभाषित करता है। भारत एक अविभाज्य संघ है जिसमें राज्यों को अपनी सीमाओं या अस्तित्व को बदलने का संवैधानिक अधिकार नहीं है।

question: Which of the following is related to the fundamental duties ?  (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Citizens of India
All the people living in India including foreigners these
Foreign tourists
None of these
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Citizens of India

Explanation:
The Fundamental Duties are enshrined in Part IV A of the Indian Constitution under Article 51A. These duties apply only to the citizens of India, not to foreigners or tourists. Originally, 10 duties were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, later increased to 11 by the 86th Amendment in 2002. These duties reflect moral and civic responsibilities, such as respecting the Constitution, national flag, national anthem, protecting the environment, etc. Fundamental duties are non-justiciable in nature, but the government can make laws to enforce them.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Under which Article are Fundamental Duties mentioned? → Article 51A
☛ Which Amendment added Fundamental Duties? → 42nd Amendment (1976)
☛ How many Fundamental Duties are there? → 11
☛ To whom do Fundamental Duties apply? → Only to citizens of India
☛ Which Amendment added the 11th duty? → 86th Amendment (2002)
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन मौलिक कर्तव्यों से संबंधित है? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: भारत के नागरिक
भारत में रहने वाले सभी लोग, जिनमें विदेशी भी शामिल हैं, इन सभी को भारत में रहने वाले सभी लोगों को
विदेशी पर्यटक
इनमें से कोई नहीं
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है भारत के नागरिक

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV A में अनुच्छेद 51A के अंतर्गत मौलिक कर्तव्य निहित हैं। ये कर्तव्य केवल भारत के नागरिकों पर लागू होते हैं, न कि विदेशियों या पर्यटकों पर। मूल रूप से 1976 में 42वें संशोधन द्वारा 10 कर्तव्य जोड़े गए थे, जिन्हें बाद में 86वें संशोधन (2002) द्वारा 11 कर्तव्य किया गया। ये कर्तव्य नैतिक और नागरिक जिम्मेदारियों को दर्शाते हैं, जैसे संविधान का सम्मान, राष्ट्रगान, राष्ट्रीय ध्वज का सम्मान, पर्यावरण संरक्षण आदि। मौलिक कर्तव्य मूल रूप से गैर-न्यायिक हैं, लेकिन सरकार इन्हें लागू करने के लिए कानून बना सकती है।

question: Which majority can be amended in parliamentary laws? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: By the absolute majority
By the absolute majority in Parliament
By Effective Majority
By the general majority of parliament
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is By the general majority of parliament

Explanation:
Under Articles 107 and 108 of the Indian Constitution, to pass ordinary laws, a simple majority of the members present and voting in each House of Parliament is required. This means that more than half of the members present and participating in the vote must support the bill. It is important to note that an absolute majority refers to more than 50% of the total membership of the House, which is a different process. For amending parliamentary laws, a simple majority is sufficient, unless the Constitution specifically requires another type of majority. Thus, ordinary bills and amendments need a simple majority to be passed.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Majority required for ordinary laws → Simple majority of members present and voting
☛ Meaning of absolute majority → More than 50% of total membership
☛ Majority for constitutional amendments → Special majority (2/3 members present and voting)
☛ Article 107 → Procedure for passing bills
☛ Article 368 → Procedure for constitutional amendments
question_hi: संसदीय कानूनों में संशोधन किस बहुमत से किया जा सकता है? (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 1)
options_hi: पूर्ण बहुमत से
संसद में पूर्ण बहुमत से
प्रभावी बहुमत से
संसद के सामान्य बहुमत द्वारा
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संसद के सामान्य बहुमत द्वारा

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 107 और 108 के तहत, सामान्य कानूनों को पारित करने के लिए संसद के दोनों सदनों में उपस्थित और मतदान करने वाले सदस्यों का सामान्य बहुमत आवश्यक होता है। इसका अर्थ है कि किसी भी सदन में उपस्थित और मतदान में भाग लेने वाले सदस्यों में से आधे से अधिक का समर्थन होना चाहिए। यह ध्यान देने योग्य है कि पूर्ण बहुमत का अर्थ सदन की कुल सदस्यता का 50% से अधिक होता है, जो कि एक अलग प्रक्रिया है। संसदीय कानूनों में संशोधन के लिए सामान्य बहुमत पर्याप्त होता है, जब तक कि संविधान में विशेष रूप से किसी अन्य बहुमत का उल्लेख न किया गया हो। इस प्रकार, साधारण विधेयकों और संशोधनों को पारित करने के लिए सामान्य बहुमत की आवश्यकता होती है।

question: In the schedule of the Indian Constitution, the provision of distribution of powers between the Center and the states has been done? (RPF SI 2018 (12/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Seventh Schedule
Fifth Schedule
10th Schedule
Sixth Schedule
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Seventh Schedule

Explanation:
The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides for the distribution of powers between the Centre and states. It contains three lists: Union List (100 subjects for Centre), State List (61 subjects for states), and Concurrent List (52 subjects for both). This forms the basis of the federal structure. The Fifth Schedule deals with scheduled areas, the Sixth Schedule with tribal areas, and the 10th Schedule with anti-defection laws.

☛ Total subjects in the Seventh Schedule? → 213 (Union: 100, State: 61, Concurrent: 52)
☛ Some subjects in the Concurrent List? → Education, Forests, Labour Welfare
☛ Which Schedule is related to defection? → 10th Schedule
☛ What does the Fifth Schedule deal with? → Administration of Scheduled Areas
question_hi: भारतीय संविधान की अनुसूची में केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच शक्तियों के वितरण का प्रावधान किया गया है? (RPF SI 2018 (12/01/2019) Shift 1)

पांचवीं अनुसूची
10वीं अनुसूची

भारतीय संविधान की सातवीं अनुसूची में केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच शक्तियों के वितरण का प्रावधान है। इसमें तीन सूचियाँ हैं: संघ सूची (केंद्र द्वारा बनाए जाने वाले 100 विषय), राज्य सूची (राज्यों द्वारा बनाए जाने वाले 61 विषय) और समवर्ती सूची (दोनों द्वारा बनाए जाने वाले 52 विषय)। यह संघीय ढाँचे का आधार है। पाँचवीं अनुसूची अनुसूचित क्षेत्रों से, छठी अनुसूची जनजातीय क्षेत्रों से और 10वीं अनुसूची दल-बदल विरोधी कानून से संबंधित है।

Religion, race, gender, or birthplace
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Religion, race, gender, or birthplace

Explanation:
Article 15 of the Indian Constitution is a fundamental right that prohibits the state from discriminating against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth. It is an extension of the right to equality (Article 14) and aims to ensure social justice. This article also prohibits discrimination in access to public places, shops, hotels, and entertainment venues. However, it allows the state to make special provisions for women, children, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other backward classes. Article 15 is crucial for promoting equality and preventing discrimination based on personal characteristics. It reinforces the secular and inclusive nature of the Indian Constitution.

Nineth

solution:

Explanation:

solution:

question: Which article is included under the 9th Schedule of Indian Constitution?  (RPF SI 2018 (12/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Article 102
Article 4
Article 243
Article 31 - B
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 31-B

Explanation:
The 9th Schedule of the Indian Constitution was added by the First Amendment (1951). It includes acts that are protected from judicial review on the ground of violation of Fundamental Rights. Originally, it contained land reform laws. Article 31-B is specifically associated with the 9th Schedule. It states that any act listed in the 9th Schedule cannot be challenged in any court for infringing Fundamental Rights. However, in the I.R. Coelho case, the Supreme Court ruled that laws in the 9th Schedule are subject to the basic structure doctrine and can be reviewed if they violate Fundamental Rights under the basic structure. Other options: Article 4 deals with reorganization of states, Article 243 with Panchayati Raj, and Article 102 with disqualification of MPs.

question: The Constitution of Fundamental Rights of Indian Constitution has been taken from which Constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (12/01/2019) Shift 1)

Constitution of South Africa
Constitution of the United States
Constitution of France
solution:

Explanation:
The Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution are inspired by the Constitution of the United States. The US Constitution includes the Bill of Rights and civil liberties, which were adapted as Fundamental Rights in India. India also adopted the concept of judicial review from the US model. Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III (Articles 12-35) of the Indian Constitution and are justiciable and enforceable. Among the other options, the Constitution of England is unwritten and a source of the parliamentary system; the Constitution of South Africa emphasizes equality and dignity; and the Constitution of France influenced republican and secular ideals in India.

question: The maximum number of members of the Council of Ministers was determined by the Constitution Amendment Act?  (RPF SI 2018 (12/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: 91st Constitutional Amendment
99th Constitution Amendment
86th Constitution Amendment
97th Constitution Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 91st Constitutional Amendment

Explanation:
The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act (2003) determined the maximum number of members of the Council of Ministers. According to Article 164(1A), the total number of ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a state shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that state. For the Union, Article 75(1A) states that the total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Lok Sabha. This amendment was enacted to control the size of the cabinet and ensure political stability. It came into effect on January 1, 2004.

question: In the Indian Parliament, the Prime Minister is appointed by which house of Parliament? (RPF SI 2018 (12/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Only by the Upper House
At the discretion of the President
Only by the Lower House
Higher or lower can be done by any House.

Explanation:
According to Article 75 of the Indian Constitution, the Prime Minister is appointed by the President. The President appoints the person who, in their opinion, is the leader of the majority in the Lok Sabha. This appointment is not made by either house of Parliament but is based on the President's discretion. However, the Prime Minister must prove majority support in the Lok Sabha. question: What type of veto (veto) does the President have in relation to any state act which has been stopped by the Governor?  (RPF SI 2018 (12/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Pocket Prohibition
Absolute Prohibition
Suspension Prohibition
Eligible Prohibition
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Absolute Prohibition

Explanation:
The President has three types of veto power over state bills: absolute veto, suspension veto, and pocket veto. When a Governor reserves a state bill for the President's consideration, the President can exercise an absolute veto, meaning he can completely reject the bill, and the state legislature cannot override it. This power comes under Articles 200 and 201 of the Indian Constitution. However, the President may also return the bill for reconsideration or grant assent. An absolute veto is the strongest form where the bill is rejected outright and cannot be passed again by the state legislature.

question: What is the right to delimitation of constituencies can be done by the majority? (RPF SI 2018 (12/01/2019) Shift 1)
options: Full majority
General majority
Effective majority
Specific majority
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is General majority

Explanation:
Under Articles 82 and 327 of the Indian Constitution, delimitation of constituencies is done by Parliament through legislation. It requires a general majority (simple majority) of members present and voting, not a special majority. Delimitation aims to readjust constituencies based on population changes. Since it is a legislative function, the Constitution does not mandate a specific majority. A general majority ensures that the law is passed by more than half of the members voting, making it a flexible process for periodic revisions.

question: What is the right to life in the Indian constitution?  (RPF SI 2018 (12/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: Basic Manual
State Policy Director's Principle
Fundamental Duty
Fundamental Rights
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fundamental Rights

Explanation:
The right to life under Article 21 of the Indian Constitution is a Fundamental Right. It protects individuals from arbitrary deprivation of life, ensures the right to live with dignity, and safeguards personal liberty. The Supreme Court has given it a broad interpretation, including aspects such as education, health, clean environment, and livelihood. This distinguishes it from Directive Principles of State Policy, which are non-justiciable. The right to life is interconnected with other fundamental rights like equality and freedom of speech. It is not absolute and can be restricted by lawful procedures. This right is essential for the protection of individual freedom and human dignity.

question: Which languages are mentioned in the Constitution for the editing of Parliament? (RPF SI 2018 (12/01/2019) Shift 2)
options: English and Tamil
Urdu and English
Hindi and Urdu
Hindi and English
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Hindi and English

Explanation:
Under Article 120 of the Indian Constitution, the business in Parliament can be conducted in Hindi and English. Similarly, Article 210 provides for state legislatures. For the editing and publishing of parliamentary documents and proceedings, these two languages are primarily used. It is important to note that this is separate from the Eighth Schedule languages. The Constituent Assembly designated Hindi as the official language while retaining English as an associate language for a transitional period. Editing here refers to the language used in preparation and publication of parliamentary records. Historically, both Hindi and English have been the primary languages for legislative functioning. This provision ensures accessibility and continuity in parliamentary work across the country.

question: What is the defense against the arbitrariness of arrest is called protection against personal freedom?  (RPF SI 2018 (12/01/2019) Shift 2)

Mendems (paramas)
Probation
Habeas Corpus (Habeas Corp)
solution:

Explanation:
Habeas corpus is a fundamental constitutional remedy that protects an individual from unlawful or arbitrary arrest. It is a writ issued by a court ordering the person who has been arrested to be produced before the court. Its purpose is to ensure that no one is detained without legal process. This right is a cornerstone of personal liberty and can be invoked under Articles 32 and 226 of the Indian Constitution. It is a powerful tool of judicial review that provides immediate relief against arbitrary detention and is considered the strongest safeguard against arbitrary state action.

question: President of India is elected- (RPF SI 2018 (16/01/2019) Shift 3)

By States

solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is By the members of Legislative Assembly of Members and States from both Houses of Parliament

Explanation:
The President of India is elected indirectly. The electoral college consists of elected members of both Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) and elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of states. This system is based on the principle of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote. The election is conducted by the Election Commission of India and the voting is secret. The value of each vote is determined based on the population of the state, ensuring equal representation. Article 54 of the Constitution provides for the election of the President. Members of Legislative Councils are not part of the electoral college. This system balances the representation of the Centre and the states.

भारत के राष्ट्रपति का चुनाव अप्रत्यक्ष रूप से होता है। इसमें मतदाता संसद के दोनों सदनों (लोकसभा और राज्यसभा) के निर्वाचित सदस्य तथा राज्यों की विधानसभाओं के निर्वाचित सदस्य होते हैं। यह प्रणाली एकल संक्रमणीय मत द्वारा आनुपातिक प्रतिनिधित्व के सिद्धांत पर आधारित है। राष्ट्रपति का निर्वाचन निर्वाचक मंडल (Electoral College) द्वारा किया जाता है, जिसमें विधान परिषदों के सदस्य शामिल नहीं होते। यह सुनिश्चित करता है कि राष्ट्रपति को राष्ट्रीय और राज्य स्तर का व्यापक प्रतिनिधित्व प्राप्त हो। संविधान के अनुच्छेद 54 के अनुसार, राष्ट्रपति के चुनाव में मतों के मूल्य की गणना जनसंख्या के आधार पर की जाती है।
